Create a polished but buildable low-poly 3D game asset concept contact sheet for CityX, a contemporary city reclamation strategy game. Soft warm daylight, muted ivory concrete, faded sage roofs, dusty brick, blue-gray glass, restrained faceted trees, matte flat-color materials, simple planar architecture and modular details that a small procedural GLB model can reproduce. No photorealistic textures, no ornate fantasy, no huge neon, no voxel pixels. White-warm-gray studio background, four evenly separated panels in a 2x2 arrangement, each contains a complete isolated rectangular ground-and-building diorama seen from the SAME elevated southeast orthographic camera about 45 degrees above ground. The dioramas should be recognizably modern functional urban facilities, distinguishable from ordinary housing/factories. Show full footprint with grass, paths, realistic door/window proportions, human silhouettes 1.75m and occasional cars about 4.6m long and adult trees 6-8m tall for scale, subtle contact shadows. Ground plot size includes yards and ancillary objects; buildings must occupy only a plausible fraction of each plot. Each panel has only its exact short English name and nominal footprint caption in neat understated typography below it. These are planning concept renders, not claimed measured CAD. Do not add interfaces, gameplay icons, control borders, fog, weapons, or logos. Keep architectural details sparse and clear enough for both top-down and oblique play.
SHEET 1, CIVIC LIFE. Top left caption '01 CITY HALL — 120 x 140 m': a dignified contemporary municipal hall, a three-to-four-story 65m x 35m symmetrical civic building about 20m tall, central recessed entrance and restrained pale stone columns, shallow hipped sage roof, broad public forecourt with low flagpoles, fountain, steps, trees, no palace dome. Top right caption '02 COMMUNITY CENTER — 60 x 80 m': an approachable two-story 35m x 22m neighborhood facility about 9m tall, L-shaped low wings, recognizable broad multiuse hall roof with skylights, covered entrance, small planted courtyard, benches, outdoor tables and a small basketball half court, NOT rows of residential houses, no grand ceremony. Bottom left caption '03 SCHOOL — 120 x 160 m': three-story 60m-long classroom wing with repetitive windows about 14m high, perpendicular short administration wing, low gymnasium, school gate, shaded gathering courtyard, one basketball court; reserve open rear yard, no oversized full stadium. Bottom right caption '04 ATHLETICS GROUND — 160 x 120 m': a low open sports campus, dusty red oval running loop around green playing field, compact small bleachers, separate basketball court and tiny changing-room pavilion, no enormous stadium stands. This is a separate modular facility that can later attach to a school, its nominal track layout is a visual game concept, not regulation sports engineering.
